game: LV @ NO Week 3 2026 (kickoff/venue/spread/total not in pack)

script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is a tendency script, not a market script. LV has given Ashton Jeanty 44 carries for 150 yards in two games and NO has allowed 4.96 YPC with 9 runs of 10+ and DT Christen Miller out, so the Raiders' path is a Jeanty ground game with Kirk Cousins. The Saints' path is the pass: Chris Olave 23 targets/268 yards/338 air, DeVaughn Vele 16/133/132, Juwan Johnson 11/120/88, against a LV defense at 10.7 YPA in the middle and without S Treydan Stukes. Base case is competitive and mixed: LV runs, NO throws, no blowout flag.
script.flip1: NO blitzes at 29% and Cousins has been bad vs pressure (LV EPA/db -0.15 vs blitz, +0.20 vs none). LV falls behind, Jeanty's carries shrink toward the 48-yard game, and check-downs (Mayer, Jeanty, Bech) rise. If NO then leads big and clocks it with Etienne/Kamara/Miller, Olave and Johnson routes get cut late.
script.flip2: Jeanty controls the clock against the soft NO front, NO plays from behind, Travis Etienne's 8.5 carries die further, and Olave/Vele/Johnson targets rise. A true LV blowout is the lower-probability version of this flip and would also risk Saints starter snaps; it cannot be sized without a spread.

injury_fallout: LV S Treydan Stukes is Out (concussion), the only named coverage absence; that helps NO deep and middle targets (Olave, Vele, Johnson), not a charted corner. LV TE Brock Bowers is Questionable (knee) with no 2026 games, so Michael Mayer (11 targets, 55 yards, logs 32 and 23) keeps the TE role unless Bowers is active on a snap count; Mayer has no saved price. NO DT Christen Miller is Out (toe), a small efficiency bump for Jeanty and Etienne. NO WR Barion Brown is Out (hamstring), depth only, targets stay with Olave/Vele. NO CB Martin Emerson is Questionable (shoulder): if he sits, LV outside WRs (Tucker 193 air yards, Nailor) face a backup, but he is not ruled out. LV DE Kwity Paye is Questionable (illness), not an out. LV QB Aidan O'Connell is Questionable (personal); Cousins is the QB in the stat pack (3 carries, rush prop). Sources: pack injury report and weeks 1-2 usage. Final inactives not in pack.

matchup.shell: Man/zone and MOFO/MOFC are not in the pack. Location splits only: LV allows left 7.43 YPA (23 att), middle 10.7 (10 att), right 6.38 (21 att). NO allows left 6.7 (27), middle 7.8 (15), right 5.3 (27).
matchup.pressure: NO blitzes 29%; LV EPA/db is -0.15 vs blitz and +0.20 clean, so pressure is the Raiders' offensive risk and a deep-shot killer for Tre Tucker. LV blitzes only 21%; NO EPA/db is +0.07 vs blitz and +0.12 clean, so Shough is not blitz-allergic in this sample.
matchup.bleeds: LV bleeds the middle (10.7 YPA on 10 throws) and has 6 passes of 20+ (pack mark 6/62; denominator ambiguous). NO bleeds the run (4.96 YPC, 9 runs of 10+) more than the pass (right side 5.3 YPA is the toughest zone; 20+ pass mark 4/73).
matchup.overlap: NO's primary target is Olave (23 targets, 338 air yards) into a secondary missing Stukes, which fits explosives more than the soft middle. The cleaner overlap is Juwan Johnson, the lead receiving TE (11 targets, 120 yards on only 88 air, so YAC), into that 10.7 middle. LV's overlap the other way is Jeanty's 22 carries into NO's 4.96 YPC front with Miller out; that is real but script-dependent and was not kept as a leg.

form: Avoiding season averages; only weeks 1-2. Olave logs 182 and 86, both over 76.5, on 11.5 targets/game; the 182 is a spike risk, the 86 cleared by only 9.5. Johnson logs 54 and 66, both well over 35.5, more stable than Olave. Vele 69 and 64, both over 49.5, but no price. Jeanty rush 102 and 48 vs 69.5 (split) at 3.41 YPC on 44 carries. Etienne rush 46 and 25 vs 39.5 in a committee (Kamara 9/15, Miller 9/30, Shough 12/32). Kamara last4 shows a single 15-yard rush game, so his 24.5 line is a role the pack does not explain. Tucker 27 and 119 vs 41 is boom/bust. Bech 23 and 25 vs 14.5 on only 6 targets. Nailor 27 and 9 vs 24.5 with 91 air yards and only 36 receiving yards.

edge_players.kills_it: The 10-attempt middle split is noise and LV sits on the TE, Johnson's YAC (120 on 88 air) regresses through 35.5, or NO leads big and clocks out his routes. A late Bowers return does not directly steal this role, but a Shough dud would.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost because two games were the whole case and the coin-flip numbers were the regression. Olave's 182 was a spike LV did not need a star safety to prevent, the down game was only 86, and the outside splits (7.43 and 6.38) were never the 10.7 middle. Johnson's 54 and 66 were YAC that a rally-to-the-flat defense took away, and 10 middle attempts at 10.7 YPA was one or two plays, not a scheme hole. Or NO got ahead and ran Etienne, Kamara, and Miller, cutting routes, which the missing spread cannot rule out. Weather, final inactives, and coverage charting were never in the pack, so a game-time Emerson/Bowers/Paye decision or an uncharted bracket is the miss step 3 and step 4 could not close. The counter is strong enough to refuse a stake and to treat Olave as droppable; it is not stronger than Johnson's target-plus-middle read, which is why that leg is flagged rather than deleted.
slip_story: One story only: Saints pass volume into a LV secondary missing Stukes, with Johnson as the middle/YAC piece and Olave as the air-yard piece. They win together and lose together, so this is one bullet, not two. Do not add a game under, a Tucker deep over (NO's 29% blitz and Cousins' -0.15 EPA vs blitz is the opposite script), or Jeanty rush over in the same slip (that leg needs LV to stay on schedule, which dies in the blitz flip that can still feed this stack). No TDs, one market per player.
